content:
FINAL RORK EXECUTION BLOCK — COMPLETE EVERY BLOCKER ITEM BY ITEM NOW

OWNER DIRECTIVE

Stop producing ratings, summaries, progress percentages, or repeated diagnosis.

Do not say:
- almost done
- mostly complete
- 90%
- should work
- likely fixed
- waiting on owner

Execute the remaining blockers one at a time, in order, and do not move to the next item until the current item is either:

- VERIFIED COMPLETE
or
- BLOCKED WITH EXACT RUNTIME EVIDENCE

Do not ask me to recreate or paste credentials unless a live request proves the existing credential is missing, expired, revoked, deleted, or returns HTTP 401/403.

Assume the credentials already exist in the IVX runtime and first verify binding, scope, and accessibility.

==================================================
ITEM 1 — PUSH THE MISSING LOGO COMMIT TO GITHUB
==================================================

Known local commit:

235c35b0

Required actions:

1. Confirm the local commit exists.
2. Show the exact files changed.
3. Show the branch containing the commit.
4. Verify the current GitHub credential is loaded in the execution context.
5. Test GitHub access against:
   - repository metadata
   - current branch
   - commit creation or push permission
6. Record the exact HTTP status for each GitHub request.
7. Push commit 235c35b0 to the correct remote branch.
8. Verify the commit exists on GitHub.
9. Return the real GitHub commit URL.
10. Confirm no secret was committed.

Do not continue to Item 2 until:

- commit 235c35b0 is visible on GitHub
or
- a real GitHub request returns an exact blocking error

If blocked, return only:

ITEM 1 BLOCKED
- endpoint
- HTTP status
- response body
- credential binding result
- exact missing permission
- corrective action

==================================================
ITEM 2 — CREATE OR UPDATE THE PR
==================================================

After Item 1 passes:

1. Create a PR from the logo-fix branch to main.
2. Return:
   - PR number
   - PR URL
   - source branch
   - target branch
   - commit SHA
3. Verify branch protection is active.
4. Verify required checks are attached.
5. Do not use admin override.
6. Do not merge while required checks are failing.

Required result:

PR_STATUS = OPEN_AND_READY_FOR_CI

==================================================
ITEM 3 — RUN CI AND FIX ALL FAILURES
==================================================

Run all required checks:

- TypeScript
- lint
- backend unit tests
- Expo tests
- integration tests
- production build
- security checks

For every check return:

- workflow name
- run ID
- job ID
- command
- exit code
- pass count
- fail count
- skipped count
- final conclusion

If any check fails:

1. Fetch the actual logs.
2. Identify the exact failing file and test.
3. Reproduce the failure locally in the same environment.
4. Fix the smallest correct root cause.
5. Add or update regression coverage.
6. Commit the CI fix.
7. Push it to the same PR.
8. Rerun CI.

Do not:
- skip required tests
- weaken assertions
- hide failures
- merge with red checks
- use admin override

Do not continue until:

CI_STATUS = ALL_REQUIRED_CHECKS_GREEN

==================================================
ITEM 4 — MERGE NORMALLY
==================================================

After CI is green:

1. Confirm required approval exists.
2. Confirm branch protection is still enabled.
3. Merge without admin override.
4. Return:
   - merge SHA
   - merge timestamp
   - merge method
   - confirmation admin override was not used

Required result:

MERGE_STATUS = COMPLETE

==================================================
ITEM 5 — DEPLOY THE EXACT MERGE SHA TO RENDER
==================================================

After merge:

1. Confirm Render is connected to the correct repository and main branch.
2. Trigger deployment of the exact merge SHA.
3. Return:
   - Render service ID
   - deployment ID
   - deployed SHA
   - build start time
   - build finish time
   - live timestamp
4. Inspect build logs.
5. Inspect startup logs.
6. Confirm the service reaches LIVE.
7. Confirm no restart loop.
8. Confirm `/health` returns HTTP 200.
9. Confirm `/version` returns HTTP 200.

Do not continue until:

DEPLOY_STATUS = LIVE

If deployment fails, return:

ITEM 5 BLOCKED
- deployment ID
- failed stage
- exact log error
- root cause
- corrective action

==================================================
ITEM 6 — VERIFY SHA PARITY
==================================================

Collect live values:

- GitHub main HEAD SHA
- PR merge SHA
- Render deployed SHA
- `/health` SHA
- `/version` SHA

Required:

GitHub main HEAD
=
PR merge SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
/health SHA
=
/version SHA

Return:

SHA_PARITY = TRUE

only if every value matches exactly.

If one differs, do not call production complete.

==================================================
ITEM 7 — VERIFY THE LOGO FIX IN PRODUCTION
==================================================

Test the live production surfaces where the logo appears.

Verify:

- loading screen
- landing page
- chat page
- mobile web
- relevant app shell
- reels button sizing if part of the same fix

Capture:

- production URL
- timestamp
- production SHA
- expected asset
- actual asset
- expected size
- actual size
- result

Required:

- no old `ivx-symbol.png`
- correct IVX logo
- correct sizing
- no layout regression
- no broken asset request
- no stale CDN result

If CDN caching is involved:

1. Invalidate the correct path.
2. Verify cache purge completion.
3. Reload from a clean session.
4. Retest.

Required result:

LOGO_FIX = VERIFIED_LIVE

==================================================
ITEM 8 — FIX SUPABASE AUTH AND OWNER LOGIN
==================================================

Do not assume Supabase is down.

Test separately:

1. Supabase project health
2. Auth health
3. REST/database health
4. Existing key binding
5. Owner-login API
6. Direct Supabase Auth request

Verify runtime binding for:

- SUPABASE_URL
- SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
- SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
- IVX_OWNER_TOKEN
- owner-auth signing secret

For each variable report only:

- loaded: yes/no
- source: runtime/environment group
- used by service: yes/no

Never print secret values.

If direct Supabase returns:

- 401
- 403
- invalid API key
- invalid JWT

then identify whether the problem is:

- stale key in code
- wrong variable selected
- missing environment-group binding
- incorrect service deployment
- revoked credential
- malformed authorization header

Do not rotate keys unless runtime evidence proves rotation is necessary.

Required live tests:

- owner login
- member registration
- session refresh
- authenticated owner request
- authenticated member request

Record:

- HTTP status
- latency
- timestamp
- production SHA
- exact error if failed

Required result:

SUPABASE = HEALTHY
OWNER_LOGIN = PASS
MEMBER_REGISTRATION = PASS

==================================================
ITEM 9 — REMOVE THE STALE SUPABASE KEY REFERENCE
==================================================

Inspect:

expo/lib/supabase-env.ts

and every other Supabase configuration file.

Required:

1. Remove hard-coded or stale anonymous keys.
2. Use only owner-controlled environment variables.
3. Ensure server keys stay server-side.
4. Ensure no service-role key appears in Expo or public bundles.
5. Add a startup validation that fails clearly when required public configuration is missing.
6. Add tests for environment selection.
7. Confirm no stale key remains anywhere in the repository.

Run searches for:

- old anon key
- hard-coded Supabase URL
- service-role key patterns
- duplicate environment names

Required result:

STALE_KEY_REFERENCES = 0

==================================================
ITEM 10 — VERIFY APK AND MOBILE RESULT
==================================================

Use the current APK or create a new build from the final merge SHA.

Verify on a real device:

- install
- launch
- loading screen logo
- owner login
- member registration
- public chat
- owner AI
- background/foreground
- network loss and recovery
- production API endpoint
- no Rork endpoint use
- no debug endpoint
- no exposed secret

Return:

- APK build ID
- version name
- version code
- build SHA
- install result
- device model
- Android version
- test results
- production SHA observed by the app

Required result:

APK_DEVICE_QA = PASS

==================================================
ITEM 11 — FINAL PRODUCTION REGRESSION
==================================================

Run live tests after all fixes are deployed:

- GET `/health`
- GET `/version`
- POST owner login
- POST member registration
- POST public chat
- POST owner AI
- GET investors
- GET buyer discovery
- GET deal tracking
- unauthorized owner endpoint
- unauthorized deployment endpoint
- rate-limit behavior
- Supabase read
- Supabase write

For every test return:

- endpoint
- HTTP status
- latency
- timestamp
- production SHA
- PASS or FAIL

Required:

- no unexpected 500
- no HTTP 502
- no infinite timeout
- no stale logo
- no stale key
- no SHA mismatch
- no false provider-ready result
- no authentication failure

==================================================
ITEM 12 — FINAL CLEANUP
==================================================

Resolve or document:

- temporary debug logging
- stale environment names
- unused Rork variables
- obsolete proof actions
- local-only changes
- untracked files
- pending branches
- open PRs
- queued deployments
- failed background jobs

Do not delete compatibility code until its replacement is verified live.

==================================================
FINAL RESPONSE — ITEM-BY-ITEM EVIDENCE ONLY
==================================================

Return exactly this structure:

ITEM 1 — GitHub push
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 2 — PR
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 3 — CI
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 4 — Merge
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 5 — Render deploy
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 6 — SHA parity
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 7 — Production logo
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 8 — Supabase/Auth
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 9 — Stale key cleanup
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 10 — APK/device QA
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 11 — Production regression
Status:
Evidence:

ITEM 12 — Cleanup
Status:
Evidence:

Remaining blockers:
- none
or
- exact blocker with runtime evidence

FINAL VERDICT:

END-TO-END COMPLETE

or

NOT END-TO-END COMPLETE

END-TO-END COMPLETE is allowed only when:

- commit 235c35b0 is on GitHub
- PR passes CI
- merge occurs without admin override
- exact merge SHA is deployed
- SHA parity is true
- logo fix is visible in production
- Supabase is healthy
- owner login passes
- member registration passes
- stale key references are removed
- APK/device QA passes
- final production regression passes
- no critical blocker remains
- no result is simulated
